discovery.greenfield_assessment: No existing codebase or documentation. All components must be built from scratch. Architecture decisions driven by kb-L0-enterprise-architecture (EA1-EA20) and kb-L2-payments-domain (PD1-PD25).

api_standards.json_conventions: camelCase properties, ISO 8601 dates, enums as strings

backend: Solution scaffold (4 projects: Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Api)
CI pipeline (lint, build, test, SAST, SCA, Docker)

architecture_decisions.title: Clean Architecture with CQRS for backend
architecture_decisions.context: Need separation of concerns, testability, and scalability for a lending platform
architecture_decisions.decision: Use .NET 8 Clean Architecture (Domain→Application→Infrastructure→Api) with MediatR CQRS
architecture_decisions.consequences: More initial setup but better maintainability. Each handler is independently testable.

architecture_decisions.title: Kotlin/Jetpack Compose for mobile
architecture_decisions.context: Need modern Android UI framework with good accessibility support
architecture_decisions.decision: Use Kotlin 2.0 + Jetpack Compose + Material Design 3 + Hilt DI
architecture_decisions.consequences: Compose-first approach. No XML layouts. All UI in Kotlin.
architecture_decisions.kb_reference: EA1 Technology Stack, EA10 Mobile Architecture

architecture_decisions.title: JWT with device-bound refresh tokens
architecture_decisions.context: Mobile app needs secure session management per SAMA requirements
architecture_decisions.decision: JWT RS256 access tokens (15-min), refresh tokens (24hr, device-bound), stored in EncryptedSharedPreferences
architecture_decisions.consequences: Short-lived access tokens reduce risk. Device binding prevents token theft.

architecture_decisions.title: In-memory database for development
architecture_decisions.context: Need fast local development without SQL Server dependency
architecture_decisions.decision: EF Core InMemoryDatabase for dev, SQL Server for staging/prod
architecture_decisions.consequences: Dev starts instantly. Some EF Core features (transactions, raw SQL) behave differently in-memory.

architecture_decisions.title: Design system before features
architecture_decisions.context: All screens need consistent look and feel from day one
architecture_decisions.decision: Build design system (tokens + atoms) in Sprint 1 before any feature screens
architecture_decisions.consequences: Sprint 1 has more infrastructure work but Sprint 2+ moves faster.

risks.risk: SMS gateway integration may delay OTP delivery in Sprint 1
risks.mitigation: Use mock SMS service for dev/staging. Real integration can be swapped via DI.

risks.risk: Sprint 1 has 57 story points — may be aggressive for a new team
risks.mitigation: Scaffold stories (US-001, US-003) can be done by senior devs in parallel. Design system (US-002) can start day 1.

risks.risk: Biometric auth (US-008) requires physical device testing
risks.mitigation: Use Android emulator fingerprint simulation for CI. Manual test on device before sprint review.

dependency_order: F-01.2 (API scaffold) and F-01.1 (mobile scaffold) can start in parallel on day 1. F-01.3 (auth) depends on both scaffolds. F-01.4 (products) depends on API scaffold. Auth and products can run in parallel once scaffolds are ready.
reasoning: Greenfield discovery for EP-01. Architecture decisions driven by EA1 (tech stack), EA2 (patterns), EA5 (security), EA10 (mobile), EA11 (design system). Domain context from PD1 (lending lifecycle — product discovery is the first step), PD18 (product configuration — BridgeNow params). Sprint 1 establishes the foundation that all subsequent sprints build on. The key risk is Sprint 1 velocity — mitigated by parallelising scaffold work.
